title: Steampunk Camera Product Showcase in Bedroom Setting
description: A virtual product photography studio set inside a minimalistic modern bedroom. The user positions a steampunk camera on a nightstand, adjusts its orientation, cycles through different dramatic lighting presets, toggles a depth-of-field bokeh effect, and captures a stylized product snapshot that is displayed in a floating polaroid-style frame.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap with ES modules from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads two GLB assets: a minimalistic modern bedroom scene and a steampunk camera model. Place the bedroom as the environment backdrop. Position the steampunk camera on a flat surface in the bedroom such as a nightstand or desk, scaled appropriately so it looks like a product on display. Set the Three.js perspective camera at a comfortable viewing angle facing the camera product. Use OrbitControls with constrained vertical rotation (10-80 degrees polar) and limited zoom range so the user always sees the bedroom context. Implement these interactions: (1) DRAG TO REPOSITION: the user can click and drag the steampunk camera model along the surface plane (raycasting onto a horizontal plane at the surface height) to reposition it on the furniture. (2) ROTATE PRODUCT: right-clicking and dragging on the steampunk camera rotates it around its Y-axis so the user can view it from different angles. (3) LIGHTING PRESETS: add an HTML button panel with 4 lighting presets — 'Warm Sunset' (orange-tinted directional + warm ambient), 'Cool Studio' (white key light + blue fill), 'Dramatic Noir' (single harsh spotlight with deep shadows using shadow maps), and 'Neon Accent' (magenta and cyan point lights). Clicking each button smoothly transitions lights over 0.5 seconds using TWEEN or manual lerp in the animation loop. (4) BOKEH TOGGLE: add a toggle button that enables or disables a simple UnrealBloomPass from Three.js post-processing to simulate a dreamy product-photo glow around the camera. (5) CAPTURE SNAPSHOT: add a 'Capture' button that calls renderer.domElement.toDataURL(), creates a floating plane with the captured texture displayed as a polaroid-style frame (white border mesh) that animates into view with a slight rotation. Add ambient light at 0.3 intensity, enable renderer shadow maps, and set tone mapping to ACESFilmicToneMapping. Include a subtle environment map using PMREMGenerator with a simple scene for reflections on the steampunk camera's metallic parts.
